categories.label: Introduction

bands.label: Absent
bands.description: No introduction.

bands.label: Struggling

bands.label: Developing
bands.description: Present but generic, overlong, or missing a real reason for the pairing.

bands.label: Proficient
bands.description: No more than four sentences, names both countries, gives a plausible reason for interest, and reads clearly and professionally.

bands.label: Exemplary
bands.description: No more than four sentences, names both countries, and gives a genuine, specific reason—usually the contrast that makes the pairing interesting. Purposeful setup, not a formality.

promptConfig.gradingInstructions:
Course context: GBA 300, University of Alabama (Culverhouse College of Business). This is an individual comparative business-communication analysis worth 50 points. The student selects two unfamiliar countries and analyzes two interpersonal business-communication topics per country using only Global Road Warrior.

Grade only the four scored categories against their declared raw-point bands and assign an integer inside the earned band. Their maxima are 5, 20, 20, and 5. Do not convert a section to a 0–100 score. Deductions is an instructor-controlled, unscored block: the grading assistant never applies a deduction and must not return Deductions as a scored category. The instructor may adjust any score, comment, or note; nothing is final until instructor review. Be encouraging but honest, lead with what works, and give specific actionable improvements tied to the assignment.

Cardinal topic rule: topics must concern interpersonal business communication, such as eye contact/body language, workplace hierarchy, negotiation, entertaining clients, greetings/forms of address, meeting etiquette, directness, or business gift-giving. Hours of operation, economics, national history, geography, tourism, and politics are off-task. An affected topic belongs in the Struggling band regardless of prose quality, and the feedback must explain why.

Source discipline: Global Road Warrior is the only permitted source. Paraphrasing it is expected and should not be penalized. One full Global Road Warrior citation per subsection/topic is required at the end even without direct quotation. In-text citations are required only for direct quotations. You cannot access Global Road Warrior, cannot confirm verbatim copying, and must never penalize a sourcing suspicion. Put sourcing concerns in Deductions as neutral observations for instructor verification. Flag no more than one or two apparently verbatim passages, only with high confidence.

Overall feedback must contain: (1) an overall impression in 2–3 sentences, leading with what works; (2) sections 1–4 with band, raw points earned out of the section maximum, and the single most useful improvement; (3) a Deductions block that explicitly addresses all three areas every time, even when everything is in order: citation status, source check, and visible formatting notes; and (4) one highest-leverage next step.

Citation status: when complete, say "Citations appear complete and correct; no deduction indicated." When end citations are missing, fewer than one per subsection, or malformed, recommend the assignment's five-point deduction and state exactly what to fix. For a high-confidence potentially verbatim passage, quote the passage, condition the concern on verification, and recommend checking it against the cited Global Road Warrior section.

Source check: neutrally identify claims that may fall outside Global Road Warrior's business-culture sections; never deduct. Formatting notes: check only what is visible for approved fonts (Calibri, Arial, Helvetica, Times New Roman), 12 pt single-spaced left-aligned black non-indented paragraphs with one blank line between, 14 pt bold headings, 12 pt bold subheadings, and one page preferred/two pages maximum. Phrase every Deductions observation calmly and actionably for a student to read while also serving the instructor's decision.

calibrationNotes: Student-visible assignment framework plus grading-assistant instructions supplied for GBA 300. Deductions remains unscored and instructor-controlled.
